title: Scaffold yencoding crate (Cargo.toml, lib.rs, error.rs)
description:
Create crate skeleton in yencoding/ directory. Add to workspace Cargo.toml.

Cargo.toml: name=yencoding, version=0.1.0, edition=2021, license=MIT OR Apache-2.0, rust-version=1.75
Dependencies: crc32fast = '1' (for CRC32 verification)
Optional dep: serde = '1' (feature=serde, for Serialize/Deserialize on public types)

error.rs: YencError enum:
  NoHeader                          -- no =ybegin line found in input
  InvalidHeader { field: String }   -- =ybegin/=ypart/=yend line missing required field or unparseable value
  CrcMismatch { expected: u32, actual: u32 }  -- decoded bytes do not match pcrc32= or crc32=
  UnexpectedEof                     -- =yend line never found
All variants: Debug, Display (describe what went wrong and what the caller should do), std::error::Error. Non-exhaustive.

lib.rs: crate-level doc covering:
- What yEnc is, who invented it (Juergen Helbing, 2001), why it exists (1-2% overhead vs 33% for base64)
- The two use cases: single-part and multi-part Usenet articles
- Relationship to uuencoding crate (same workspace, different encoding)
- NZB is out of scope -- link to concept, note crate does not parse NZB
- Security note: decoded output size approximately equals encoded input size (no decompression bomb risk from the encoding itself); however decoded bytes may be a compressed archive and any subsequent decompression is the caller's responsibility
- Quick-start example for decode() and encode()
close_reason: Scaffolded: Cargo.toml, lib.rs, error.rs, header.rs, decode.rs, encode.rs. Added to workspace.
